correctness.rationale: The top boundary-incidence Gram matrix has the exact oriented form L=nI−ss^T. For even n, the affinely centred columns split as the orthogonal free sum of two regular (m−1)-simplices: the product of their polars gives r=n/sqrt(2m(m−1)), while vertex barycenter averaging gives unique enclosing radius sqrt(n(n−2)). For odd n, the simplex barycentric functionals λ_i(x)=x_i/n+s_i(1−1·x/n) have two intrinsic facet gradient norms sqrt(n−1)/n and sqrt(n+3)/n; the sum of normalized slacks yields the unique optimal incenter and r, and the p-positive-vertex barycenter gives the uniquely minimal enclosing ball and strict q-negative-vertex deficit. All centres lie in the affine hull. Both parity asymptotics and almost-equal edge-length contrast follow from exact formulas.
